messages:
jordan_sales: Hey — Acme wants an explicit plan for USB delivery (sneakernet). Questions: can we sign bundles with HSM-backed keys, what's the SLA for signed hotfixes, and how do we handle SBOM delivery and acceptance testing offline?
talia_se: Short answers: yes to HSM signing (we sign CI artifacts with HSM and can produce detached sigs), hotfix SLA depends on support tier (standard: 72h, enterprise: 24h), and SBOM can be shipped as part of the bundle or as a separate manifest file.
ben_sre: Ops caveat: if we sign with our CA, customer must import our root into their offline trust store, or we can provide an on-site signing token flow where their ops signs with a customer key we validate. Both are supported but different SOW language.
kim_legal: From contracts: we can offer either (a) Redwood-signed bundles with audit trail, or (b) an offline signing kit that hands control to customer. Option (b) shifts liability; we need a waiver + acceptance checklist.
emily_pmo: Acme specifically asked if we will bill when we hand the USB to their courier or when they confirm apply. They prefer flat monthly device maintenance for offline nodes.
talia_se: Recommended commercial model: charge for bundle issuance for each major release + optional per-device maintenance covering N deltas/month. Billing on applied upgrade is tricky since we don't always get apply confirmation offline.\en
talia_se: (typo above) Sorry — billing on applied upgrade is possible if they run a 'redwood-apply-report' which issues a signed receipt uploaded later; otherwise bill on delivery.
ben_sre: Technical: we strongly recommend chunked content for large model files (split into parts with manifest + per-part checksums). Provide a resumable apply utility and total estimated apply time (e.g., 45-90 mins depending on disk and model size). Add sample validation cmds:
```
# verify all checksums and detached signature
sha256sum -c redwood-bundle.manifest && openssl dgst -sha256 -verify redwood_pub.pem -signature bundle.sig bundle.tar.gz
# dry-run apply
./redwood-apply --bundle bundle.tar.gz --verify --dry-run
```
jordan_sales: They asked about emergency hotfix turnaround: can we guarantee signed artifact within 24h and courier dispatch same day?
ben_sre: We can guarantee signed artifact within 24h on enterprise SLA. Courier dispatch depends on customer's logistics. We'll add an "expedited signing" fee and an ops checklist to coordinate pickup windows.
kim_legal: I'll draft clause: "Emergency Signed Artifact" available within 24 hours subject to expedited fee and customer confirmation of pickup logistics; Redwood not liable for transit delay. Also include export-control & cryptography disclosure.
emily_pmo: For acceptance testing, propose a 72h acceptance window after apply with a signed acceptance report (optional). If they fail acceptance, we provide rollback support and one remediation delta free.
talia_se: Rollback mechanics: every apply creates a pre-apply snapshot and a rollback token. Command example:
```
./redwood-apply --bundle b.tar.gz --snapshot /var/redwood/snap-20240301 && ./redwood-apply --rollback-to snap-20240301
```
ben_sre: Note: if model quantization or format changes, KV cache invalidation may be required; include migration step or stash/restore instructions in runbook.
jordan_sales: Can someone drop a 1-page ops checklist + SOW wording here by EOD? Acme wants to sign before EOW. :pray:
artifact-bot: artifact-bot: ticket SALES-8123 created (deliverables: ops-checklist, SOW language for offline signing options, expedited signing fee schedule, SBOM delivery format).
ben_sre: I'll post the ops checklist draft in ~3 hrs (include commands, expected durations, traces to capture).
kim_legal: I'll post the contract snippets for both signing options and the emergency modifier by EOD.
jordan_sales: Perfect — thanks all. I'll consolidate and send to Acme once drafts are in. :thumbsup:
